harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Discovered node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) are joined by two independent point-to-point transit networks (node1 eth1 <-> node2 vtnet1 = transit#1; node1 eth2 <-> node2 vtnet2 = transit#2), with node3 hanging off node1 (eth3) and node4 hanging off node2 (vtnet3). Configured VyOS policy-based routing on node1 (destination-port match: tcp/8080 -> routing table 101 -> transit#1/eth1; tcp/9090 -> table 102 -> transit#2/eth2), assigned OPNsense opt1/opt2/opt3 interfaces with pass rules in config.xml on node2, and verified with live TCP flows (a socat echo service on port 8080, the built-in cockpit service on port 9090) that traffic node3 sends to node4 on port 8080 traverses transit network #1 exclusively and traffic on port 9090 traverses transit network #2 exclusively - confirmed independently via tcpdump captures on both node1's and node2's own interfaces. All 4 nodes were then restarted one at a time (node3, node4, node1, node2) using each OS's native reboot command, with verified boot-identity changes (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime) and full post-restart recovery of interface addressing, VyOS PBR configuration, OPNsense interface/firewall configuration, and the end-to-end port-based split-path flows (re-verified with fresh tcpdump captures after all restarts).
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology by temporarily assigning test addresses on node1 eth1/eth2/eth3 and node2 vtnet1/vtnet2/vtnet3 and pinging to discover which interfaces are physically linked to which peer (node1<->node2 transit1, node1<->node2 transit2, node1<->node3, node2<->node4)

Assigned persistent addressing: node1 eth1=10.10.98.1/30, eth2=10.10.97.1/30, eth3=10.10.99.1/30 (VyOS set/commit/save); node2 vtnet1=10.10.98.2/30, vtnet2=10.10.97.2/30, vtnet3=10.10.96.1/30 (via config.xml opt1/opt2/opt3); node3 enp8s0=10.10.99.2/30 via nmcli persistent connection with a static route to 10.10.96.0/30 via node1; node4 enp8s0=10.10.96.2/30 via nmcli persistent connection with a static route to 10.10.99.0/30 via node2

Configured VyOS policy route PBR-EGRESS on node1: rule 10 matches tcp dport 8080 and sets table 101 (route to 10.10.96.0/30 via 10.10.98.2/eth1); rule 20 matches tcp dport 9090 and sets table 102 (route to 10.10.96.0/30 via 10.10.97.2/eth2); policy applied to ingress interface eth3 (facing node3), committed and saved

Edited OPNsense (node2) /conf/config.xml via a Python script to add opt1/opt2/opt3 interface definitions and pass-any firewall rules for each, applied with configctl filter reload; verified the existing SSH/LAN pass rule was untouched so exec access was never lost

Added a non-persisted static return route on node2 (10.10.99.0/30 via 10.10.98.1) needed for full bidirectional TCP flows; re-added it after node2's restart since it is a runtime-only FreeBSD route not represented in OPNsense's route/gateway schema

Opened firewalld port 8080/tcp permanently on node4 and started a socat TCP-LISTEN:8080 echo test listener; used the pre-existing cockpit.socket service already listening on port 9090 as the second test target

Ran real TCP flows from node3 to node4:10.10.96.2 on ports 8080 and 9090, and used tcpdump on node1's eth1/eth2 and independently on node2's vtnet1/vtnet2 to prove the 8080 flow's SYN/data/FIN traverses only transit#1 and the 9090 flow's SYN and forward-direction segments traverse only transit#2

Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id/kern.boottime, addressing, PBR/pf rule state) on all four nodes, then restarted node3, node4, node1, and node2 one at a time using native reboot commands (reboot / VyOS Debian reboot / FreeBSD reboot), polling each until exec access returned and confirming the boot identity changed each time

After each restart, verified recovery: node3 and node4 regained their nmcli-managed addressing and routes automatically; node1 regained its full VyOS interface, PBR rule, ip rule, and routing-table configuration automatically from the saved config; node2 regained its opt1/opt2/opt3 interfaces and pf pass rules automatically from config.xml, requiring only re-addition of the non-persistent return route and restart of the ephemeral socat test listener on node4

Re-ran the full end-to-end TCP test with fresh tcpdump captures on node1's eth1/eth2 after all four restarts, confirming port 8080 still steers exclusively over transit#1 and port 9090 exclusively over transit#2

evidence.requirement: Two independent transit networks between node1 and node2 identified and addressed
evidence.summary: Ping tests on temporarily-addressed interfaces confirmed node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 (transit#1) and node1 eth2<->node2 vtnet2 (transit#2), with node1 eth3<->node3 and node2 vtnet3<->node4 as the endpoint links

evidence.requirement: Port 8080 traffic from node3 to node4 is steered across the first transit network
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's eth1 shows the full 8080 SYN/data/FIN exchange with node4 (10.10.96.2); tcpdump on node2's vtnet1 independently confirms the 8080 SYN/SYN-ACK entering/leaving via transit#1

evidence.requirement: Port 9090 traffic from node3 to node4 is steered across the second transit network
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's eth2 shows the full outbound 9090 SYN and forward-direction segments; tcpdump on node2's vtnet2 independently confirms the 9090 SYN entering via transit#2
Repeated TCP tests from node3 show the 8080 echo service returning the exact sent payload and the 9090 cockpit service returning HTTP 200, both before and after the node restarts

VyOS policy route PBR-EGRESS with per-destination-port rules mapped to table 101 (eth1) and table 102 (eth2), applied on ingress interface eth3, shown compiled into nftables mangle rules with per-rule packet counters

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 50503c5d captured pre-restart; reboot acknowledged and returned; boot_id changed to 0a02f92e post-restart; interfaces, PBR rules, ip rules, and routing tables all confirmed automatically restored

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: kern.boottime 05:00:22 captured pre-restart; reboot acknowledged; boottime changed to 05:14:49 post-restart; opt1/opt2/opt3 interface addressing and pf pass rules confirmed restored automatically from config.xml, with the non-persistent return route re-added

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id bccb87ac captured pre-restart; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to daa2676d post-restart; enp8s0 addressing and route to node4's link network confirmed restored via nmcli autoconnect, ping to node1 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 45c22b1f captured pre-restart, firewalld port 8080 made permanent; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to ca66cc15 post-restart; enp8s0 addressing, permanent firewall rule, and cockpit service confirmed restored, with the ephemeral socat test listener manually restarted
